items.title: 3 Dividend Aristocrats Trading Below Their Historical Valuations
items.summary: Income investors rarely sell stocks that keep raising payouts, which usually keeps them pricey. Three Dividend Aristocrats broke that pattern, and each carries a different reason for the markdown, from messy cleanups to soda worries to a finished turnaround.

items.title: Hormel Yields 5.5% After a 40% Stock Decline. Is Its Dividend Safe?
items.summary: Hormel has raised its dividend for 60 straight years, but shrinking raises, a stock that lost nearly 40% of its value, and a payout that once outpaced free cash flow put the next increase in question.

items.title: Tyson Foods Yields 3.55%. Can Its Cash Flow Support Another Dividend Raise?
items.summary: Tyson's reported earnings fell short of covering its dividend bill last year, yet the company still managed to raise its payout. Whether that trick works again depends on what happens inside its business over the next few months.
